item.content:encoded:
This extends to all data recorded while the doors were closed, and so far no medium has been found which can resist this effect, save for pen and paper.

Back in the day, when computers were first a thing but paper wasn't obsolete yet, there were these machines that exported data (like datetime stamps) to paper called printers. When I read the above line, that was my first thought. Granted, using humans to log datetime stamps does make for a more interesting story but it's a little inefficient.

How about adding a computer that prints its logs onto paper along with a hefty battery? Perhaps a motion sensor camera as well that could capture any 'anomalous' movements by who knows what. If the Foundation could reliably monitor the time, they could even use it to monitor aging on other SCPs. It would be impossible to put item X in there for a specific time frame, but they could take their chances and see what happens.

item.title: Re: DOWNVOTED
item.content:encoded: I know this is a two year necro, but it must be said that one should only censor an SCP document if it makes sense to censor it. For example, it wouldn't be logical to censor the number of years the D-Class were apparently in the box. However, it might be a good idea to censor the name of the scientist who sent dozens of D-Class to their deaths. Whoever first introduced the style of censorship we use had the right idea, but it's way too frequently misused.

item.title: DOWNVOTED
item.content:encoded: For pointless, inconsequential redaction. I have a challenge for you, the same as for anyone else. Don't just go [lolhurrdurrredacted] for something you think should be unnerving or scary. Come on, challenge yourself and the reader. See if you can honestly make it creepy without being cheesy. See if you can legitimately make it a little scary to ponder the consequences of. Cuz as it stands, most of the time, it just ends up with, "Huh, well, I guess this could have been more interesting if the author had bothered to actually come up with something here." Think of something terrifying and *write* it. Ask yourself, is there a legitimate reason the number of years would be classified? We know it's less than 10. And why would the description of injuries be so horrible as to "redact" them when you can find much worse things described elsewhere? The people reading the document ostensibly see worse shit than a disembowelment most times, so put a little effort into it and come up with something that makes me either go "wow" or that makes me give a damn.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Blegh, downvoted for being really, really, really mediocre. It is well written and the tone is solid, but the idea itself just does nothing for me. It's a box that makes time flow weird….so? This lacks any kind of hook to grab and hold my attention.

Also, I know some people will disagree strongly with me, but I don't think you need to cover your ass from inquiries at every turn. The interior doesn't need to be indestructible; the Foundation probably wouldn't risk destroying the object by damaging the interior unless we have reason to believe there was something genuinely valuable to be gained in doing so. Also, why wouldn't an hourglass work (I mean both in universe and out). It is completely illogical for it to not work since really ANYTHING can be used to track time if you know how. I get that you added it, though, as a way to prevent people reading this from poking holes in it. What I don't get it what good it does the article? So what if we can record exactly what the time dilation effects are? What is the harm in that?

item.content:encoded:
Only the interior is indestructible, the exterior is as vulnerable as any standard shipping container. So if his theory is correct, you could remove the majority of the container and the portal would still work. If he's wrong, and the container is a vital piece of the object, the whole thing could go tits up.

Another reason the interior needs to be indestructible is to resist the progress of time. For all anyone knows, thousands of millennia could have passed inside the room, and any standard material would have degraded in that amount of time. I'm open to alternatives though.

item.content:encoded:
I can fix this. I'll strain out all the clichés I can, but a few of them are necessary.

1: The interior has to be indestructible, otherwise someone would punch a hole in it and take a peek outside.
2: If it's indestructible, you can't really test it thoroughly, so it's going to be unknown. What if I added a few more details about the material from non-invasive tests/observations?
3: It also has to be some kind of portal, otherwise you could punch a hole in the exterior and take a peek inside.

The impossible dimensions thing can be taken out, you're right about that.

As for the Experiment log, I did think about having the mummified guy go crazy and write stuff on the walls. The problem is, he's not in there for all eternity, only until he dies of dehydration. A few days isn't enough time to start flinging faeces, if you know what I mean. The last entry was supposed to suggest shenanigans, with the internment of multiple subjects allowing for acts of violence and cannibalism, but I went for the less is more approach. Maybe it's not quite enough. I'll try to add a few more grotesque elements.

Tomorrow, though. It's 1am and time to sleep.

item.content:encoded:
Please tell me this is a list of cliche's and related to Bright's challenge.

If not… Please go read the cliche list.

Also:

constructed from an unknown material

Here we go…

proven to be completely impervious to damage

No thank you.

impossible dimensions

There is already an SCP that does this, and is probably better than this.

the doors of the container act as a portal to the interior

There are already a city full of portal SCP's that do various weird and odd things, they are pretty much better than this

the entire Experimentation Log

Look, this does't make it more interesting nor does it tell us more about it than we already know.

To be frank, the idea of being alone and confused and frightend in a room for all eternity, isolated so that no matter how long a person screams no one can hear him, whatnot, sounds great. However, all the OTHER things tacked on detract from that potential horror, until you just have a mess of 'interesting' details that lose the core of the SCP- a box that messes with time when you shove people in it. It also brings up the question do they just sit there, do they scream or cry or scrape against the walls so hard their nails break? If it were mere after a time i would be writing 'time time time' and various clocks in various positions with my own blood evrywhere because isolation does horrible things to a psyche. If a person became a child would they remember everything that had happened to them prior to their age-change or do their memories revert? If a person stays there long enough, what happens if they need to poop or pee? What if they're hungry or thirsty?

Final Report:

SCP that buries its hook with a buncha unnecessary details. Downvoted.
